elements.element: Vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with limits of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3A contains no commercial general liability insurance requirement.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3A contains no commercial general liability insurance requirement or aggregate limit.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance with limits of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3A requires the Servicer to maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor must maintain cyber/privacy liability insurance with limits of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3A requires the Servicer, for so long as it processes Obligor data, to maintain cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Obligor data is the contract-specific data to which the conditional requirement applies.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3A contains no workers' compensation insurance requirement.

elements.element: Vendor must provide certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3A expressly requires the Servicer to provide certificates of insurance on request.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance with limits of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The required USD 2,000,000 professional liability limit exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback threshold.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor must maintain cyber/privacy liability insurance with limits of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires USD 5,000,000 of cyber liability insurance for so long as the Servicer processes Obligor data, exceeding the USD 2,000,000 fallback threshold.

result.reason: The clause satisfies the fallback because its E&O and cyber limits exceed the fallback limits. It does not satisfy the preferred position because it omits both commercial general liability and workers' compensation coverage. The amendment is not minimal for the fallback: it adds higher limits, a certificate obligation, an own-expense requirement, and a one-year post-termination tail beyond what the fallback requires. The existing expenses and risk-retention provisions remain unchanged, and no direct contradiction is introduced. Drafting is generally clear, although using “Obligor data” rather than the playbook term “Customer Data” may narrow or create ambiguity around the cyber trigger.
